video_title: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work — Aman Singh, Arca
gist: Aman Singh of Arca, a $64M AI-native wealth management firm, explains its model-agnostic in-house harness, tiered model routing, 10-day agent workflows with memory, deterministic guardrails, and human-in-the-loop execution.

insights.claim: Arca, an AI-native wealth management firm that raised $64 million, positions AI to replace all the work around the human advisor rather than the advisor, so clients only experience faster, more proactive service delivered by a human.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Template for AI-native services roll-ups: AI as back office, human as client interface.
insights.quote: the role of AI at Arca is not to replace the advisor. It is to replace all of the work around the advisor.

insights.claim: Arca argues that being the operating firm rather than a SaaS vendor lets it standardize how work is done, require staff feedback, and encode its own principles into agents, an advantage over vendors selling tools.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Full-stack AI-native firms may capture more value and iterate faster than SaaS sellers into the same industry.
insights.quote: We're actually not a SaaS company. We are we are the firm ourselves.

insights.claim: Arca's agents are designed to prompt people more than people prompt agents, running proactive 24/7 service, versus incumbent firms that equip staff with AI tools they must prompt.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Distinguishes AI-native from AI-augmented incumbents; proactive agents may be the durable differentiator.
insights.quote: agents prompt people more than people prompt agents and it is a proactive kind of service that is running for them 24/7

insights.claim: Anthropic's move into financial services is seen by Arca as validating for the industry, but Arca does not view it as direct competition because tool-equipped traditional firms differ from AI-native firms.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Lab entry into verticals may expand the market rather than commoditize AI-native operators, per this operator.

insights.claim: Agents at Arca surface proactive value such as discovering a prospect's current advisor charged undisclosed fees on top of $1,500 and was not a fiduciary, and flagging deadlines or missed RMD risks.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Fee and fiduciary transparency from document-reading agents is a competitive threat to incumbent advisors with opaque fees.

insights.claim: Arca uses frontier models, primarily Anthropic's Claude after previously using Gemini and then OpenAI, and chooses among them with internal benchmarks of its own harness capabilities.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Enterprise model choice is migrating between labs on private evals, implying low lab loyalty.

insights.claim: A recently touted model (called Luna in the transcript) scored well on external benchmarks but proved too slow and costly in Arca's internal benchmarks, illustrating external benchmark gaps.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Public benchmarks may not predict production fit; speed and cost dominate for agent workloads.
insights.quote: despite the external benchmarks claiming great things for Luna, it didn't really quite work out for us as as well as we had expected.

insights.claim: Arca routes tasks by complexity tiers: tax planning and analysis go to the heaviest tier (Opus-class or heavy GPT), while background agent activity uses lower-tier models, with the routing hidden from advisors.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Tiered routing shows high-volume background agent work is cost-sensitive and favors cheaper models.

insights.claim: Arca deliberately builds its own model-agnostic harness and declines to depend on Anthropic's managed agents, because owning memory and operational knowledge is owning the firm's intelligence.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Lab-hosted agent platforms face adoption resistance from firms that see memory and context as core IP.
insights.quote: owning that is owning your intelligence

insights.claim: Arca's agents run workflows spanning about 10 days, such as raising $100,000 for a tax bill, using per-client memory tracking current state, ownership, completed steps and next actions, plus a nightly 'dreaming' reflection that updates that memory.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Persistent memory plus reflection is the pattern enabling multi-day agent work in regulated services.

insights.claim: New signals at Arca are routed by type: replies on an existing email thread go to the agent already handling it, while a new signal such as a phone call wakes a fresh agent that reads client memory to place it in context.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Event-driven agent dispatch plus shared memory is an emerging architecture for always-on services.

insights.claim: Arca runs a nightly meta-agent over real-world traces paired with staff feedback to propose harness fixes, but keeps a human engineer in the loop because agents write bad prompt changes where every fix bloats the prompt.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Self-improving agent loops still need human gatekeepers; fully autonomous prompt optimization is not yet trusted.
insights.quote: agents will will make really nasty prompt changes if you leave them leave them do it. Um every little fix becomes the whole prompt.

insights.claim: Arca keeps its operational knowledge base as files in a first-class 'knowledge' tab that experts edit directly, with agents citing knowledge so errors surface through trace analysis.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Expert-curated, citeable knowledge bases are the practical alternative to opaque fine-tuning for domain adaptation.

insights.claim: Arca's agents can fully automate portfolio analysis but cannot move money, liquidate assets or contact clients without a human, even though its custodian provides APIs enabling it; agents currently only propose trades.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Even AI-native wealth firms keep humans on execution; autonomous trading by agents is not near-term.

insights.claim: Arca's safety layers are deterministic and sit at capability edges: LLM verification on every database write, prompt-injection screening on incoming emails and documents, and PII checks plus a consensus of small models on outbound data.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Layered deterministic plus small-model guardrails are the emerging enterprise agent security stack.

insights.claim: Arca runs agent code in a sandbox used only for offloaded computation, translating output into a strict format and discarding the code before it reaches the backend, then verifies the generated financial plan for raw account numbers and promised returns.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Code-execution agents are made safe by constraining data formats, not trusting the code.

insights.claim: Arca claims AI compliance review beats human review because it is tireless at finding even tiny non-compliant mentions, and every agent and human action is logged with what, who, where and when, giving auditability by default.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Regulated industries may see AI as improving compliance, lowering the barrier to AI adoption.
insights.quote: AI is tireless at at at finding even the smallest mention of a non-compliant um piece of writing

insights.claim: Arca finds models confidently use stale financial facts such as 2025 tax brackets, so it uses a detector that nudges them to a verified fact base or web search when financial rigor is required.
insights.speaker: Aman Singh
insights.so_what: Stale parametric knowledge is a core failure mode for finance and tax agents, creating demand for verified-data layers.
